corrections.issue: The index figures were read 'as of Wednesday' (the recording was on a Friday, upload date 26 July 2026), so they are to about 22 July, not end of July; July was a partial month, and Niels also gave July month-to-date figures that the claim omits.
corrections.fix: As of the Wednesday before the Friday recording (about 22 July 2026) the Beta 50 index was about +10% YTD (+1.34% in July), the SG CTA index +10.37% YTD (+0.89% in July), the SG Trend index +10.15% YTD (+0.94% in July) and the short-term traders index +4.52% YTD; MSCI World was +9% YTD and the US aggregate bond index -0.12% YTD.

corrections.issue: The direction of the bias is omitted. Baltas says that if thematic clusters are ignored the predicted portfolio risk is biased (he says downwards, then corrects himself to upwards), concluding that the portfolio is riskier than the model suggests. Read with 'we're more risky than what we should have been', this means the risk model understates actual risk.
corrections.fix: If thematic clusters are left out of the covariance matrix, the risk model understates the portfolio's true risk and misdistributes risk across positions (Baltas misspeaks on the direction but concludes the portfolio is riskier than reported); a theme-aware risk model (the Lee paper, tested on stocks) corrects this and the idea extends to cross-asset trend portfolios.

completeness_estimate: 0.70 - first reader captured the two main papers (Graham universe size, Run One River defence layers), the thematic/narrative arguments and the performance narrative accurately; missed the July month-to-date index numbers, client-demand comments, five-of-seven-months record, portable-alpha leverage logic (two points), the third-bucket specification, narrative life cycle and lead-lag mechanism, theme transience in covariance, the price-as-objective and price-path-as-proxy discussion, and Niels's sector-grouping scepticism
